final:
-- Phase 1 spec: 8-bit rotation. Phase 2 bodies.
-- Uses only u8 arithmetic and comparisons, so no conversion functions are needed.
-- rotr8 no longer calls rotl8 in its body, so the only cycle is through contracts,
-- and each function has a decreases clause on k.

rotl8(x: u8, k: int) -> u8 =
  pre k >= 0
  pre k <= 7
  post rotr8(out, k) == x
  ex rotl8(129, 1) == 3
  ex rotl8(1, 7) == 128
  ex rotl8(200, 0) == 200
  decreases k
  var v: u8 = x
  for i in range(0, k)
    if v >= 128
      v = (v - 128) * 2 + 1
    else
      v = v * 2
  v

rotr8(x: u8, k: int) -> u8 =
  pre k >= 0
  pre k <= 7
  post rotl8(out, k) == x
  ex rotr8(3, 1) == 129
  ex rotr8(128, 7) == 1
  decreases k
  var v: u8 = x
  for i in range(0, k)
    if v % 2 == 1
      v = v // 2 + 128
    else
      v = v // 2
  v

test_rotl8() =
  assert rotl8(129, 1) == 3
  assert rotl8(1, 7) == 128
  assert rotl8(200, 0) == 200

test_rotr8() =
  assert rotr8(3, 1) == 129
  assert rotr8(128, 7) == 1
  assert rotr8(200, 0) == 200
